newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade students continue demos but elderly hostile.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade students continue demos but elderly hostile.

text.p: Defiant students and their teachers promised on Sunday to continue protests against alleged election-rigging by Serbia's ruling socialists, but older people were hostile to Belgrade's daily demonstrations.

Ten thousand students marched in the centre of the capital to applause from bystanders after opposition parties said the supreme court had rejected their claim that they were cheated of victory in local elections on November 17.

A technical faculty teacher said outside the St Sava cathedral: "Protests are the only way to show the will of the people, because this will to change the regime could not be expressed in the elections."
The march was headed by an effigy of President Slobodan Milosevic wearing striped prison fatigues.
Although the supreme court is supposed to have had the last say, some in the crowd were optimistic they would still win redress.

"This supreme court decision is temporary," another teacher said. "Perhaps the court president will sacked, or another elegant way out found. There will surely be more purges so that Milosevic can get out of this."

Nikoleta Nikolic, a 22-year-old molecular biology student, said: "I'm not surprised by the court decision because if it had recognised the opposition victory, it would have recognised the election-rigging.
"The only person above the court is Milosevic and there is every likelihood that, as before, he will appear like a good fairy and solve everything."
Most demonstrators wanted the United States and other Western countries which have supported the opposition to keep up their pressure on the socialists.
"Even small details show that Milosevic is cracking up," a male student said. "He is susceptible to outside pressure and the greater the pressure, the more he yields."
Outside the St Sava cathedral, a 73-year-old government supporter denounced the students for "destroying their country -- they are hooligans."
A listening woman rounded on him and said: "What are you offering my young son, what is his future here? I voted for my son's future and my vote was annulled."

The elderly man replied: "I only arrived yesterday and learned from the national media that the students are destructive. They do not know how much it costs to disrupt traffic and factories. Please don't publish my name. I don't want problems."
